// file: sigma_wave_check.vr
// Σ-волна 2026-07-11: независимая verum-верификация комбинаторных ядер
// T-226 (полярный закон + томография) и T-228 (Голей Тюрина).
//
// Дисциплина M1: третья независимая реализация (после sympy и ручного
// вывода), целочисленная арифметика, только скаляры и массивы Int в
// горячих циклах (безопасная зона дефекта L-4).

// Прямые Фано в циклической маркировке: l_p = {p, p+1, p+3} mod 7.
fn line_has(p: Int, x: Int) -> Bool {
    x == p % 7 || x == (p + 1) % 7 || x == (p + 3) % 7
}

// Третья точка прямой через пару {i,j}; -1, если пары нет на прямой p.
fn third_point(i: Int, j: Int) -> Int {
    let mut k = -1;
    let mut p = 0;
    while p < 7 {
        if line_has(p, i) && line_has(p, j) {
            let mut m = 0;
            while m < 7 {
                if line_has(p, m) && m != i && m != j {
                    k = m;
                }
                m = m + 1;
            }
        }
        p = p + 1;
    }
    k
}

// ============================================================
// Часть 1: T-226 — полярный закон и точная томография (в целых
// числах: скорости 6*r целочисленны при целых gamma).
// ============================================================
fn check_t226() -> Int {
    let mut fails = 0;

    // gamma_p = p + 1  (те же значения, что и в разобранном
    // примере §3a корпусного документа)
    let mut gamma = [0; 7];
    let mut p = 0;
    while p < 7 {
        gamma[p] = p + 1;
        p = p + 1;
    }

    // G и точечные потоки T_k
    let mut big_g = 0;
    p = 0;
    while p < 7 {
        big_g = big_g + gamma[p];
        p = p + 1;
    }
    let mut t = [0; 7];
    let mut k = 0;
    while k < 7 {
        p = 0;
        while p < 7 {
            if line_has(p, k) {
                t[k] = t[k] + gamma[p];
            }
            p = p + 1;
        }
        k = k + 1;
    }

    // (a) полярный закон: 6*r_ij = G - T_{third(i,j)} для всех 21 пар,
    //     где 6*r_ij считается напрямую из определения канала.
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < 7 {
        let mut j = i + 1;
        while j < 7 {
            let mut six_r = 0;
            p = 0;
            while p < 7 {
                let mut cnt = 0;
                if line_has(p, i) { cnt = cnt + 1; }
                if line_has(p, j) { cnt = cnt + 1; }
                if cnt == 1 {
                    six_r = six_r + gamma[p];
                }
                p = p + 1;
            }
            let kk = third_point(i, j);
            if kk < 0 || six_r != big_g - t[kk] {
                print(f"FAIL polar law at pair ({i},{j})");
                fails = fails + 1;
            }
            j = j + 1;
        }
        i = i + 1;
    }

    // (б) сумма T_k = 3G  и  сумма (G - T_k) = 4G  (эквивалент
    //     G-восстановления: sum rho = (2/3) G при делении на 6)
    let mut sum_t = 0;
    k = 0;
    while k < 7 {
        sum_t = sum_t + t[k];
        k = k + 1;
    }
    if sum_t != 3 * big_g {
        print("FAIL sum T = 3G");
        fails = fails + 1;
    }

    // (в) томография в целых числах: 2*gamma_p = ((3G - сумма T по
    //     точкам прямой p) ... ) — эквивалентная целочисленная форма
    //     gamma_p = 3*(sum rho)/2 - 3*(rho-сумма по прямой):
    //     6*gamma_p = (сумма_k (G-T_k)) - 3*(сумма_{k in l_p} (G-T_k)) ...
    //     проще напрямую: из тождества T-суммы по прямой:
    //     сумма_{k in l_p} T_k = G + 2*gamma_p  =>  gamma_p восстановим.
    p = 0;
    while p < 7 {
        let mut line_t = 0;
        k = 0;
        while k < 7 {
            if line_has(p, k) {
                line_t = line_t + t[k];
            }
            k = k + 1;
        }
        if line_t - big_g != 2 * gamma[p] {
            print(f"FAIL line-sum identity at p={p}");
            fails = fails + 1;
        }
        p = p + 1;
    }

    // (г) полярное разбиение: ровно 3 пары на точку
    k = 0;
    while k < 7 {
        let mut cls = 0;
        i = 0;
        while i < 7 {
            let mut j = i + 1;
            while j < 7 {
                if third_point(i, j) == k {
                    cls = cls + 1;
                }
                j = j + 1;
            }
            i = i + 1;
        }
        if cls != 3 {
            print(f"FAIL polar class size at k={k}");
            fails = fails + 1;
        }
        k = k + 1;
    }

    fails
}

// ============================================================
// Часть 2: T-228 — Голей Тюрина. Слова кодируются 24-битными Int.
// ============================================================

// Циклический Хэмминг [7,4] с генератором 1 + x + x^3 (biti 0..6),
// расширенный битом чётности в позиции 7. Возвращает 16 слов (8-бит Int).
fn extended_hamming(g0: Int, g1: Int, g2: Int, g3: Int) -> [Int; 16] {
    let mut words = [0; 16];
    let mut msg = 0;
    while msg < 16 {
        let mut c = [0; 7];
        let mut s = 0;
        while s < 4 {
            if (msg / pow2(s)) % 2 == 1 {
                // прибавить сдвинутый генератор
                let gbits = [g0, g1, g2, g3];
                let mut d = 0;
                while d < 4 {
                    if gbits[d] == 1 {
                        let pos = (s + d) % 7;
                        c[pos] = 1 - c[pos];
                    }
                    d = d + 1;
                }
            }
            s = s + 1;
        }
        let mut w = 0;
        let mut parity = 0;
        let mut b = 0;
        while b < 7 {
            if c[b] == 1 {
                w = w + pow2(b);
                parity = 1 - parity;
            }
            b = b + 1;
        }
        if parity == 1 {
            w = w + pow2(7);
        }
        words[msg] = w;
        msg = msg + 1;
    }
    words
}

fn pow2(n: Int) -> Int {
    let mut r = 1;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < n {
        r = r * 2;
        i = i + 1;
    }
    r
}

fn popcount24(x: Int) -> Int {
    let mut c = 0;
    let mut v = x;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < 24 {
        c = c + v % 2;
        v = v / 2;
        i = i + 1;
    }
    c
}

fn xor24(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int {
    let mut r = 0;
    let mut va = a;
    let mut vb = b;
    let mut bit = 1;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < 24 {
        if (va % 2 + vb % 2) % 2 == 1 {
            r = r + bit;
        }
        va = va / 2;
        vb = vb / 2;
        bit = bit * 2;
        i = i + 1;
    }
    r
}

fn check_t228() -> Int {
    let mut fails = 0;
    let a8 = extended_hamming(1, 1, 0, 1);   // корпусной репер: 1+x+x^3
    let b8 = extended_hamming(1, 0, 1, 1);   // зеркальный: 1+x^2+x^3

    // |A ∩ B| = 2 (нуль и все-единицы)
    let mut inter = 0;
    let mut ia = 0;
    while ia < 16 {
        let mut ib = 0;
        while ib < 16 {
            if a8[ia] == b8[ib] {
                inter = inter + 1;
            }
            ib = ib + 1;
        }
        ia = ia + 1;
    }
    if inter != 2 {
        print(f"FAIL |A∩B| = {inter}, want 2");
        fails = fails + 1;
    }

    // сумма Тюрина: 4096 слов (a+x | b+x | a+b+x), веса -> энумератор
    let mut wt = [0; 25];
    ia = 0;
    while ia < 16 {
        let mut ib = 0;
        while ib < 16 {
            let mut ix = 0;
            while ix < 16 {
                let blk1 = xor24(a8[ia], b8[ix]);
                let blk2 = xor24(a8[ib], b8[ix]);
                let blk3 = xor24(xor24(a8[ia], a8[ib]), b8[ix]);
                let word = blk1 + blk2 * 256 + blk3 * 65536;
                let w = popcount24(word);
                wt[w] = wt[w] + 1;
                ix = ix + 1;
            }
            ib = ib + 1;
        }
        ia = ia + 1;
    }

    // энумератор Голея: 1 + 759 x^8 + 2576 x^12 + 759 x^16 + x^24
    if wt[0] != 1 { print("FAIL wt0"); fails = fails + 1; }
    if wt[8] != 759 { print(f"FAIL wt8 = {wt[8]}"); fails = fails + 1; }
    if wt[12] != 2576 { print(f"FAIL wt12 = {wt[12]}"); fails = fails + 1; }
    if wt[16] != 759 { print(f"FAIL wt16 = {wt[16]}"); fails = fails + 1; }
    if wt[24] != 1 { print("FAIL wt24"); fails = fails + 1; }
    let mut w = 1;
    while w < 8 {
        if wt[w] != 0 {
            print(f"FAIL nonzero weight below 8: wt[{w}]={wt[w]}");
            fails = fails + 1;
        }
        w = w + 1;
    }

    // совершенство прокола: 4096 * (1+23+253+1771) == 2^23
    let ball = 1 + 23 + 253 + 1771;
    if 4096 * ball != 8388608 {
        print("FAIL perfection arithmetic");
        fails = fails + 1;
    }

    fails
}

// ============================================================
// Часть 3: диагональные знаки, сохраняющие φ, = симплексный код (8 шт.)
// φ-условие: сумма знаков по каждой прямой чётна.
// ============================================================
fn check_simplex_diagonals() -> Int {
    let mut count = 0;
    let mut s = 0;
    while s < 128 {
        let mut ok = 1;
        let mut p = 0;
        while p < 7 {
            let b0 = (s / pow2(p % 7)) % 2;
            let b1 = (s / pow2((p + 1) % 7)) % 2;
            let b3 = (s / pow2((p + 3) % 7)) % 2;
            if (b0 + b1 + b3) % 2 == 1 {
                ok = 0;
            }
            p = p + 1;
        }
        count = count + ok;
        s = s + 1;
    }
    if count != 8 {
        print(f"FAIL simplex diagonal count = {count}, want 8");
        return 1;
    }
    0
}

fn main() {
    let f1 = check_t226();
    let f2 = check_t228();
    let f3 = check_simplex_diagonals();
    let total = f1 + f2 + f3;
    if total == 0 {
        print("SIGMA-WAVE VERUM CHECK: ALL PASS (T-226 polar law + line-sum tomography; T-228 Turyn Golay enumerator + perfection; simplex 2^3)");
    } else {
        print(f"SIGMA-WAVE VERUM CHECK: {total} FAILURES");
    }
}


// file: main.vr
// ============================================================================
// uhm_core — M1 materialization (types and measures) of the SYNARC-Omega
// specification (paper v2.2, Section 6 + Definition 3.x canon).
//
// M1 gate (paper §9): uhm_core compiles under `verum check`; the measures
// P, R, Phi, D_diff, sigma agree with the executable oracle on 10^4
// random states. The self-test below generates the states with a
// deterministic LCG so an external oracle (Python) can replay the exact
// same inputs bit-for-bit from the same seed.
//
// Canon enforced here (v2.2):
//   - purity          P   = Tr(rho^2)
//   - reflexivity     R   = 1/(7P)
//   - integration     Phi = sum_{i!=j}|g_ij|^2 / sum_i g_ii^2   (R-3 canonical)
//   - integration_l1        (logged diagnostic ONLY, no threshold semantics)
//   - Coh_E               = (g_EE^2 + 2 sum_{j!=E}|g_Ej|^2) / Tr(rho^2)
//                           (axiom-septicity HS-projection, range [1/7, 1])
//   - D_diff (7D form)    = 1 + 6 * Coh_E                       (Def. 3.5)
//   - sigma_k             = clamp(1 - 7 g_kk, 0, 1)
//   - Fano channel        : populations fixed, coherences x 1/3 (T-110);
//                           continuous form e^{-r_ij dt},
//                           r_ij = (1/6) sum_{|line cap {i,j}| = 1} gamma_p
//   - regeneration        : exact affine exponential,
//                           alpha = 1 - e^{-kappa v dt}  (CPTP for all dt)
// ============================================================================

mount core.math.elementary.{sqrt, exp, ln};
mount core.math.coding.fano_lines;

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Constants (theorems of UHM, not hyperparameters)
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

const EPS: Float = 1e-12;

/// Critical purity P_crit = 2/7 (T-160).
const P_CRIT: Float = 0.2857142857142857;
/// Reflection threshold R_th = 1/3 (T-40b).
const R_TH: Float = 0.3333333333333333;
/// Integration threshold Phi_th = 1 (T-129).
const PHI_TH: Float = 1.0;
/// Differentiation minimum D_min = 2 (T-151).
const D_MIN: Float = 2.0;
/// Goldilocks ceiling P_max = 3/7 (T-124).
const P_MAX: Float = 0.42857142857142855;
/// Discrete Fano cycle coherence multiplier (T-110).
const FANO_CONTRACTION: Float = 0.3333333333333333;
/// Maximum self-awareness depth (T-142).
const SAD_MAX: Int = 3;
/// Index of the E (Interiority) axis in [A,S,D,L,E,O,U].
const E_AXIS: Int = 4;

fn kappa_boot(omega_0: Float) -> Float {
    omega_0 / 7.0
}

fn clampf(x: Float, lo: Float, hi: Float) -> Float {
    if x < lo { lo } else if x > hi { hi } else { x }
}

fn softplus(x: Float) -> Float {
    if x > 20.0 { x } else { ln(1.0 + exp(x)) }
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Density7: 7x7 complex density matrix, split real/imaginary storage
// (the EpistemicState<k> pattern of core.math.quantum_logic; avoids the
// V-L1 Complex/Numeric gap). Invariants hold BY CONSTRUCTION: the only
// public constructors are from_cholesky, maximally_mixed, fano_seed,
// equal_population, and the invariant-preserving channels below.
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

type Density7 is {
    re: [Float; 49],
    im: [Float; 49],
};

implement Density7 {
    /// Gamma = L L^dag / Tr(L L^dag) from 49 real parameters:
    /// 7 softplus diagonals + 21 lower-triangle re + 21 lower-triangle im.
    public fn from_cholesky(params: &[Float; 49]) -> Density7 {
        let mut l_re = [0.0; 49];
        let mut l_im = [0.0; 49];
        for i in 0..7 {
            l_re[i * 7 + i] = softplus(params[i]);
        }
        let mut idx = 7;
        for i in 1..7 {
            for j in 0..i {
                l_re[i * 7 + j] = params[idx];
                l_im[i * 7 + j] = params[idx + 21];
                idx = idx + 1;
            }
        }
        let mut g_re = [0.0; 49];
        let mut g_im = [0.0; 49];
        for i in 0..7 {
            for j in 0..7 {
                let mut s_re = 0.0;
                let mut s_im = 0.0;
                for k in 0..7 {
                    // L[i,k] * conj(L[j,k])
                    let a_re = l_re[i * 7 + k];
                    let a_im = l_im[i * 7 + k];
                    let b_re = l_re[j * 7 + k];
                    let b_im = l_im[j * 7 + k];
                    s_re = s_re + a_re * b_re + a_im * b_im;
                    s_im = s_im + a_im * b_re - a_re * b_im;
                }
                g_re[i * 7 + j] = s_re;
                g_im[i * 7 + j] = s_im;
            }
        }
        let mut tr = 0.0;
        for i in 0..7 {
            tr = tr + g_re[i * 7 + i];
        }
        let inv = 1.0 / tr;   // tr > 0: softplus diagonals are strictly positive
        for x in 0..49 {
            g_re[x] = g_re[x] * inv;
            g_im[x] = g_im[x] * inv;
        }
        Density7 { re: g_re, im: g_im }
    }

    public fn maximally_mixed() -> Density7 {
        let mut re = [0.0; 49];
        let im = [0.0; 49];
        for i in 0..7 {
            re[i * 7 + i] = 1.0 / 7.0;
        }
        Density7 { re: re, im: im }
    }

    /// Fano-seeded diagonal state: E, O, U populated at 1/3 each (P = 1/3).
    public fn fano_seed() -> Density7 {
        let mut re = [0.0; 49];
        let im = [0.0; 49];
        re[4 * 7 + 4] = 1.0 / 3.0;
        re[5 * 7 + 5] = 1.0 / 3.0;
        re[6 * 7 + 6] = 1.0 / 3.0;
        Density7 { re: re, im: im }
    }

    /// Equal-population stratum state: diagonal 1/7, uniform real coherence c
    /// on every off-diagonal pair. PSD for c in [0, 1/7] (I/7 + c(J - I) with
    /// eigenvalues 1/7 + 6c and 1/7 - c). On this stratum Phi = 7P - 1 exactly.
    public fn equal_population(c: Float) -> Density7 {
        let mut re = [0.0; 49];
        let im = [0.0; 49];
        for i in 0..7 {
            for j in 0..7 {
                if i == j {
                    re[i * 7 + j] = 1.0 / 7.0;
                } else {
                    re[i * 7 + j] = c;
                }
            }
        }
        Density7 { re: re, im: im }
    }

    /// Fieldwise copy. Single-pointer-arg calls are the only shape that
    /// survives the L-4-family VBC defect past the GC epoch (~10^3
    /// allocations): every two-pointer-arg call (self + by-ref array)
    /// first silently aliases its result with an argument and later
    /// crashes with a corrupted argument register. See repro notes.
    public fn copy(&self) -> Density7 {
        Density7 { re: self.re, im: self.im }
    }

    public fn trace(&self) -> Float {
        let mut t = 0.0;
        for i in 0..7 {
            t = t + self.re[i * 7 + i];
        }
        t
    }

    /// P = Tr(rho^2) = sum |g_ij|^2 (Hermitian storage).
    public fn purity(&self) -> Float {
        let mut p = 0.0;
        for x in 0..49 {
            p = p + self.re[x] * self.re[x] + self.im[x] * self.im[x];
        }
        p
    }

    /// R = 1/(7P) (T-96 canon).
    public fn reflexivity(&self) -> Float {
        1.0 / (7.0 * self.purity())
    }

    /// Canonical integration (Def. 3.4, repair R-3):
    /// Phi = sum_{i!=j}|g_ij|^2 / sum_i g_ii^2. Denominator >= 1/7 by
    /// Cauchy-Schwarz on the unit trace, so the guard never fires on a
    /// valid state.
    public fn integration(&self) -> Float {
        let mut num = 0.0;
        let mut den = 0.0;
        for i in 0..7 {
            for j in 0..7 {
                let m2 = self.re[i * 7 + j] * self.re[i * 7 + j]
                       + self.im[i * 7 + j] * self.im[i * 7 + j];
                if i == j { den = den + m2; } else { num = num + m2; }
            }
        }
        num / (den + EPS)
    }

    /// L1 coherence mass — logged diagnostic ONLY (R-3 demoted this form).
    public fn integration_l1(&self) -> Float {
        let mut phi = 0.0;
        for i in 0..7 {
            for j in 0..7 {
                if i != j {
                    let m2 = self.re[i * 7 + j] * self.re[i * 7 + j]
                           + self.im[i * 7 + j] * self.im[i * 7 + j];
                    phi = phi + sqrt(m2);
                }
            }
        }
        phi
    }

    /// Coh_E = (g_EE^2 + 2 sum_{j!=E}|g_Ej|^2) / Tr(rho^2)
    /// (axiom-septicity HS-projection canon; range [1/7, 1]).
    public fn coh_e(&self) -> Float {
        let gee = self.re[E_AXIS * 7 + E_AXIS];
        let mut off = 0.0;
        for j in 0..7 {
            if j != E_AXIS {
                let m2 = self.re[E_AXIS * 7 + j] * self.re[E_AXIS * 7 + j]
                       + self.im[E_AXIS * 7 + j] * self.im[E_AXIS * 7 + j];
                off = off + m2;
            }
        }
        (gee * gee + 2.0 * off) / (self.purity() + EPS)
    }

    /// D_diff, 7D operational form (Def. 3.5): 1 + 6 Coh_E / Coh_E^max,
    /// Coh_E^max = 1.
    public fn d_diff(&self) -> Float {
        1.0 + 6.0 * self.coh_e()
    }

    /// Per-channel stress sigma_k = clamp(1 - 7 g_kk, 0, 1) (T-92).
    public fn sigma(&self) -> [Float; 7] {
        let mut s = [0.0; 7];
        for k in 0..7 {
            s[k] = clampf(1.0 - 7.0 * self.re[k * 7 + k], 0.0, 1.0);
        }
        s
    }

    public fn is_hermitian(&self) -> Bool {
        for i in 0..7 {
            for j in 0..7 {
                if (self.re[i * 7 + j] - self.re[j * 7 + i]).abs() > 1e-9 {
                    return false;
                }
                if (self.im[i * 7 + j] + self.im[j * 7 + i]).abs() > 1e-9 {
                    return false;
                }
            }
        }
        true
    }

    /// Schur (entrywise) dephasing: populations fixed, coherence (i,j)
    /// multiplied by m[i*7+j] in (0,1]. CPTP for multiplier matrices arising
    /// from commuting-projector Lindbladians (paper §6, v2.2).
    public fn dephase(&self, m: &[Float; 49]) -> Density7 {
        let mut re = self.re;
        let mut im = self.im;
        for i in 0..7 {
            for j in 0..7 {
                if i != j {
                    re[i * 7 + j] = re[i * 7 + j] * m[i * 7 + j];
                    im[i * 7 + j] = im[i * 7 + j] * m[i * 7 + j];
                }
            }
        }
        Density7 { re: re, im: im }
    }

    /// Convex mixture toward a target (the exact regeneration step with
    /// alpha = 1 - e^{-kappa v dt}; CPTP for every dt >= 0).
    public fn mix_toward(&self, target: &Density7, alpha: Float) -> Density7 {
        let a = clampf(alpha, 0.0, 1.0);
        let mut re = [0.0; 49];
        let mut im = [0.0; 49];
        for x in 0..49 {
            re[x] = (1.0 - a) * self.re[x] + a * target.re[x];
            im[x] = (1.0 - a) * self.im[x] + a * target.im[x];
        }
        Density7 { re: re, im: im }
    }
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Fano plane PG(2,2): lines l_p = {p, p+1 mod 7, p+3 mod 7}
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn fano_line(p: Int) -> [Int; 3] {
    [p, (p + 1) % 7, (p + 3) % 7]
}

fn line_contains(p: Int, q: Int) -> Bool {
    let l = fano_line(p);
    q == l[0] || q == l[1] || q == l[2]
}

/// The discrete self-observation cycle P_Fano: every coherence x 1/3 (T-110).
/// In-place, single-argument form: passing a freshly allocated multiplier
/// array by reference here trips the L-4-family VBC defect once total
/// allocations cross a GC epoch (~t 1000-3000 in this program) -- the
/// callee reads a stale register as its second pointer argument. With the
/// constant folded in and one argument, the frame shape avoids the defect.
fn fano_cycle_inplace(rho: &mut Density7) {
    for i in 0..7 {
        for j in 0..7 {
            if i != j {
                rho.re[i * 7 + j] = rho.re[i * 7 + j] * FANO_CONTRACTION;
                rho.im[i * 7 + j] = rho.im[i * 7 + j] * FANO_CONTRACTION;
            }
        }
    }
}

/// The exact continuous Fano channel e^{dt D}: coherence (i,j) decays at
/// r_ij = (1/6) sum_{p : |l_p cap {i,j}| = 1} gamma_p (uniform rates here).
/// In-place single-pointer-arg form (L-4 family workaround; see copy()).
fn fano_exponential_inplace(rho: &mut Density7, gamma: Float, dt: Float) {
    for i in 0..7 {
        for j in 0..7 {
            if i != j {
                let mut r = 0.0;
                for p in 0..7 {
                    let on_i = line_contains(p, i);
                    let on_j = line_contains(p, j);
                    if on_i != on_j { r = r + gamma / 6.0; }
                }
                let m = exp(0.0 - r * dt);
                rho.re[i * 7 + j] = rho.re[i * 7 + j] * m;
                rho.im[i * 7 + j] = rho.im[i * 7 + j] * m;
            }
        }
    }
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Deterministic LCG (shared with the Python oracle): x' = (a x + c) mod 2^31
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

type Lcg is {
    state: Int,
};

implement Lcg {
    public fn new(seed: Int) -> Lcg {
        Lcg { state: seed % 2147483648 }
    }

    public fn next(&mut self) -> Int {
        self.state = (1103515245 * self.state + 12345) % 2147483648;
        self.state
    }

    /// Uniform in [-1, 1]. Deliberately NOT implemented as a wrapper over
    /// self.next(): a nested &mut-receiver call in a hot loop triggers VBC
    /// defect L-4 (repro/uhm_nested_mut_receiver_call.vr) — pointer-register
    /// corruption in a later by-ref method call.
    public fn uniform(&mut self) -> Float {
        self.state = (1103515245 * self.state + 12345) % 2147483648;
        (self.state as Float) / 2147483648.0 * 2.0 - 1.0
    }
}

// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// M1 self-test: invariants + exact laws on 10^4 LCG states, plus an
// oracle digest (first 3 states, all measures) for external replay.
// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn main() {
    // LCG inlined as a plain local: any &mut-receiver method called from
    // this loop trips VBC defect L-4 (see repro); plain locals are safe.
    let mut rng_state = 20260710;
    let n_states = 10000;
    let mut fails = 0;
    let mut sum_p = 0.0;
    let mut sum_r = 0.0;
    let mut sum_phi = 0.0;
    let mut sum_phi1 = 0.0;
    let mut sum_ce = 0.0;
    let mut sum_d = 0.0;
    let mut sum_sig = 0.0;

    // Cross-check against the INDEPENDENT stdlib coding module. The cyclic
    // labeling {p, p+1, p+3} and the Hamming(7,4) weight-3 codewords are
    // BOTH Fano planes on 7 points but under different labelings (related
    // by a PGL(3,2) relabeling), so we compare structure, not sets:
    // 7 lines, every line has 3 points, every pair of lines meets in
    // exactly one point, every point lies on exactly 3 lines.
    let code_lines = fano_lines();
    if code_lines.len() != 7 {
        print(f"FAIL coding.fano_lines count: {code_lines.len()}");
        fails = fails + 1;
    }
    let mut struct_ok = true;
    for p in 0..7 {
        let lp = fano_line(p);
        // line has 3 distinct points
        if lp[0] == lp[1] || lp[1] == lp[2] || lp[0] == lp[2] { struct_ok = false; }
        for q in 0..7 {
            if q != p {
                let lq = fano_line(q);
                let mut inter = 0;
                for a in 0..3 {
                    for b in 0..3 {
                        if lp[a] == lq[b] { inter = inter + 1; }
                    }
                }
                if inter != 1 { struct_ok = false; }
            }
        }
    }
    for point in 0..7 {
        let mut on = 0;
        for p in 0..7 {
            if line_contains(p, point) { on = on + 1; }
        }
        if on != 3 { struct_ok = false; }
    }
    if !struct_ok {
        print("FAIL Fano incidence structure");
        fails = fails + 1;
    }

    // Pre-loop exact-law checks (run at LOW allocation count: two-pointer
    // calls after the GC epoch are compromised by the L-4-family defect).
    // Stratum anchoring: Phi = 7P - 1 exactly on the equal-population stratum.
    let strat = Density7.equal_population(0.09);
    let sp = strat.purity();
    let sphi = strat.integration();
    if (sphi - (7.0 * sp - 1.0)).abs() > 1e-9 {
        fails = fails + 1;
        print(f"FAIL stratum anchoring: Phi={sphi} vs 7P-1={7.0 * sp - 1.0}");
    }
    // Regeneration: the exact convex mix lands on the target at alpha = 1.
    let seed_state = Density7.fano_seed();
    let mixed = strat.mix_toward(&seed_state, 1.0);
    if (mixed.purity() - seed_state.purity()).abs() > 1e-12 {
        fails = fails + 1;
        print("FAIL regeneration endpoint");
    }

    for t in 0..n_states {
        let mut params = [0.0; 49];
        for x in 0..49 {
            rng_state = (1103515245 * rng_state + 12345) % 2147483648;
            params[x] = (rng_state as Float) / 2147483648.0 * 2.0 - 1.0;
        }
        let rho = Density7.from_cholesky(&params);

        let p = rho.purity();
        let r = rho.reflexivity();
        let phi = rho.integration();
        let phi1 = rho.integration_l1();
        let ce = rho.coh_e();
        let d = rho.d_diff();
        let s = rho.sigma();

        // Invariants
        if (rho.trace() - 1.0).abs() > 1e-9 { fails = fails + 1; print(f"FAIL trace at {t}"); }
        if !rho.is_hermitian() { fails = fails + 1; print(f"FAIL hermitian at {t}"); }
        if p < 1.0 / 7.0 - 1e-9 || p > 1.0 + 1e-9 { fails = fails + 1; print(f"FAIL purity range at {t}: {p}"); }
        if (r * 7.0 * p - 1.0).abs() > 1e-9 { fails = fails + 1; print(f"FAIL R identity at {t}"); }
        // Global range of Coh_E is [0, 1]; the 1/7 floor holds only on the
        // No-Zombie viable class (T-38a) — the corpus range note attributes
        // the minimum to I/7, which is the VIABLE-class minimizer, not the
        // global one (E-orthogonal pure states reach 0). Corpus fix filed.
        if ce < 0.0 - 1e-12 || ce > 1.0 + 1e-9 { fails = fails + 1; print(f"FAIL Coh_E range at {t}: {ce}"); }
        if d < 1.0 - 1e-9 || d > 7.0 + 1e-9 { fails = fails + 1; print(f"FAIL D range at {t}: {d}"); }
        if (d - (1.0 + 6.0 * ce)).abs() > 1e-12 { fails = fails + 1; print(f"FAIL D formula at {t}"); }
        for k in 0..7 {
            if s[k] < 0.0 - 1e-12 || s[k] > 1.0 + 1e-12 { fails = fails + 1; print(f"FAIL sigma range at {t}"); }
        }

        // Continuous channel at the cycle time equals the discrete cycle:
        // gamma * tau = (3/2) ln 3  =>  multiplier e^{-(2/3) gamma tau} = 1/3.
        // (Run BEFORE the in-place cycle below, while rho is untouched.)
        // Channel exact laws are exercised in the SAFE ZONE only (t < 500,
        // below the GC epoch): past ~2x10^3 iterations the L-4-family VBC
        // defect makes struct-returning calls alias their arguments (the
        // copy() result aliases rho; the in-place channel then mutates rho
        // through the alias), so any channel test out there tests the
        // defect, not the law. Measures return scalars and stay reliable;
        // the invariant checks above would flag construction corruption.
        if t < 500 {
            // T-110 exact law: the discrete cycle multiplies every
            // coherence by 1/3, hence canonical Phi contracts by exactly
            // 1/9 (numerator x 1/9, denominator fixed).
            let mut cyc = rho.copy();
            fano_cycle_inplace(&mut cyc);
            let phi_c = cyc.integration();
            if (phi_c - phi / 9.0).abs() > 1e-9 * (1.0 + phi) {
                fails = fails + 1;
                print(f"FAIL T-110 Phi-contraction at {t}: {phi_c} vs {phi / 9.0}");
            }
            // Continuous channel at the cycle time equals the discrete
            // cycle: gamma tau = (3/2) ln 3 => multiplier 1/3.
            if t % 100 == 0 {
                let tau = 1.5 * ln(3.0);
                let mut cont = rho.copy();
                fano_exponential_inplace(&mut cont, 1.0, tau);
                let phi_cont = cont.integration();
                if (phi_cont - phi_c).abs() > 1e-9 * (1.0 + phi) {
                    fails = fails + 1;
                    print(f"FAIL cycle-time identity at {t}");
                }
            }
        }

        sum_p = sum_p + p;
        sum_r = sum_r + r;
        sum_phi = sum_phi + phi;
        sum_phi1 = sum_phi1 + phi1;
        sum_ce = sum_ce + ce;
        sum_d = sum_d + d;
        for k in 0..7 {
            sum_sig = sum_sig + s[k];
        }

        // Oracle digest for external replay (plain comparison: an extra
        // decremented local here collides with a callee argument register
        // in the VBC frame allocator -- L-4 family, see repro notes)
        if t < 3 {
            print(f"ORACLE {t} P={p} R={r} PHI={phi} PHI1={phi1} COH_E={ce} D={d} S0={s[0]} S6={s[6]}");
        }
    }

    print(f"CHECKSUM P={sum_p} R={sum_r} PHI={sum_phi} PHI1={sum_phi1} COH_E={sum_ce} D={sum_d} SIG={sum_sig}");

    if fails == 0 {
        print(f"M1 SELFTEST PASS: {n_states} states, all invariants and exact laws hold");
    } else {
        print(f"M1 SELFTEST FAIL: {fails} failures");
    }
}

# uhm_core — M1 materialization (SYNARC-Omega)

The first materialized cog of the SYNARC-Omega blueprint
(`../../paper/synarc-omega-spec.pdf`, v2.2): the 7x7 density-matrix carrier
and the canonical UHM measures, per gate **M1** of paper §9.

## Gate M1 status: PASSED (2026-07-11)

1. `verum check` — clean (research profile: refinement types + SMT).
2. Self-test (`verum run`, interpreter tier): 10^4 deterministic-LCG random
   states; all invariants (trace, Hermiticity, purity range, R-identity,
   Coh_E/D ranges, D-formula, sigma ranges) and exact laws hold:
   - T-110: discrete Fano cycle multiplies every coherence by exactly 1/3,
     canonical Phi contracts by exactly 1/9;
   - cycle-time identity: continuous channel at gamma*tau = (3/2) ln 3
     equals the discrete cycle;
   - stratum anchoring: Phi = 7P - 1 on the equal-population stratum;
   - regeneration endpoint: exact convex mix lands on target at alpha = 1;
   - Fano incidence structure cross-checked against the independent
     `core.math.coding` stdlib module (structural: 7 lines, pairwise
     single-point intersection, 3 lines per point; the cyclic and Hamming
     labelings differ by a PGL(3,2) relabeling).
3. External oracle (`oracle/m1_oracle.py`): independent Python replay of the
   same LCG + Cholesky + measures; all seven aggregate checksums agree
   (five bit-exact, two within 1e-10 relative), per-state digests agree to
   1e-12.

Reproduce:

    verum check
    verum run > run.log
    python3 oracle/m1_oracle.py run.log

## Canon (paper v2.2)

- `integration()` is the canonical HS-ratio Phi (repair R-3); the L1 form
  survives only as the logged diagnostic `integration_l1()`.
- `d_diff()` is the 7D operational form 1 + 6*Coh_E (Def. 3.5, PW canon).
- `coh_e()` — HS-projection form; **global range [0,1]**, viable floor 1/7
  (T-38a). The M1 self-test exposed a corpus range misstatement
  ([1/7,1] attributed to I/7 as global minimum) — fixed in the corpus
  (axiom-septicity + 4 claim-site files, EN+RU) on 2026-07-11.
- Fano channel: exact closed-form exponentials (paper §6 v2.2), coherence
  (i,j) rate r_ij = (1/6) * sum over lines hitting exactly one endpoint.

## Toolchain caveats (on the record)

- **L-4** (found by this gate; repro
  `verum/repro/uhm_nested_mut_receiver_call.vr`): past a GC epoch
  (~10^3-10^4 allocations) the VBC interpreter makes struct-returning calls
  alias their arguments (silent wrong numerics), then corrupts argument
  registers (crash). Scalar-returning calls stay reliable. The self-test
  therefore confines channel-law checks (struct copies) to a low-allocation
  safe zone (t < 500) and keeps the 10^4-state loop scalar-only.
- **L-3**: AOT emits const-zero stubs; the gate runs on the interpreter tier.

## Layout

- `src/main.vr` — constants, `Density7` (from_cholesky / maximally_mixed /
  fano_seed / equal_population; purity, reflexivity, integration,
  integration_l1, coh_e, d_diff, sigma; dephase, mix_toward), Fano plane
  (lines, cycle, exact exponential), LCG, M1 self-test.
- `oracle/m1_oracle.py` — independent replay oracle.

M2 (dynamics: Strang integrator + event-driven runtime under the
interpreter tier) is the next gate; the module split into
`uhm_core.{constants,density,fano}` follows with it.

% Appendix D: Complete Verum API reference

\section{Complete Verum API reference}
\label{app:verum-api}

This appendix gives the complete public API of \SYNARC{} as seven Verum
cogs. Each cog exports a module whose public interface is listed here.
This appendix is the authoritative \emph{normative} reference for API
names, types, and contracts; the cogs themselves are materialized
through gates M1--M3 of \S\ref{subsec:impl-status}, and no claim of a
distributed source tree is made before those gates flip (ledger item
I-8). Two grounding facts matter for the reader: the quantum substrate
this API refines already ships in the Verum standard library
(\texttt{core.math.quantum\_logic}: \texttt{EpistemicState<k>} ---
density matrices with Hermiticity, PSD and unit trace,
\texttt{CptpChannel<k>}, L\"uders measurement, Uhlmann fidelity, Bures
distance, von~Neumann entropy), so \texttt{DensityMatrix7} below is a
thin refinement of \texttt{EpistemicState<7>} rather than a from-scratch
matrix layer; and the syndrome layer of Appendix~K ships as
\texttt{core.math.coding}. Opaque type exports are shown with their
carrier elided (\texttt{is \{ /* internal */ \}}).

\begin{notebox}[Intuition --- how to read this API as a developer]
The whole runtime is seven cogs, and they stack in dependency order rather than
sprawl. At the bottom sits \texttt{uhm\_core}: the density-matrix type and the
four consciousness measures, which everything else imports and which depends on
nothing in return. Above it the dynamics cogs --- the Fano dissipator, the
regeneration channel, the Strang integrator --- turn one state into the next;
above them the cognitive cogs (the Kan-complex levels, the modalities, the
self-model) and the sensorimotor and learning cogs that couple the mind to a
world. Two facts save a reader real work. First, \texttt{DensityMatrix7} is not a
new matrix library --- it is a thin refinement of the Verum standard library's
\texttt{EpistemicState<7>}, which already ships Hermiticity, positivity, unit
trace, fidelity, Bures distance and entropy, so this API adds the \emph{seven}
specialisation and the UHM contracts, not the linear algebra underneath. Second,
every signature carries its law in its type: a \texttt{requires} line is a
precondition the caller must meet, an \texttt{ensures} line a guarantee the SMT
backend has already checked --- so the contract you read is the contract the
compiler enforces, with no gap between the documentation and the obligation.
\end{notebox}

\subsection{Cog \texttt{uhm\_core}}
\label{subsec:api-core}

\begin{lstlisting}[caption={\texttt{uhm\_core} public API.},label={lst:api-core}]
module uhm_core;

// ============================================================================
// Error hierarchy (categorically forced: one variant per failure mode)
//
// Justification: every CPTP channel, every Lindblad step, every Kan
// extension can fail in precisely one of these structurally distinct
// ways. The variants are exhaustive by the completeness theorem
// T-Completeness-of-Coverage: each of the 12 categorical obligations
// has exactly one failure mode, plus numerical edge cases.
// ============================================================================

public type SynarcError is
    /// CPTP invariant violated: Hermiticity, PSD, or trace-1 broken.
    /// Source: StrangIntegrator, RegenerationChannel, FanoDissipator.
    CptpViolation { property: Text, expected: Float, actual: Float }
    /// Purity dropped below P_crit = 2/7 -- death spiral initiated.
    /// Source: ConsciousnessVerifier, v_gate.
  | PurityCollapse { p: Float, p_crit: Float, tau: Float }
    /// Bures distance computation produced NaN (sqrt of negative).
    /// Source: bures_distance, bures_fidelity.
  | BuresNaN { rho_trace: Float, sigma_trace: Float }
    /// Kan horn filler failed: no CPTP-compatible extension exists.
    /// Source: inf_n, left_kan, right_kan.
  | HornFillerFailed { level: Int, missing_index: Int }
    /// L-III topology modification corrupted epistemic site.
    /// Source: update_topology, add_theory.
  | TopologyCorrupted { reason: Text, snapshot_id: Int }
    /// Neurogenesis trigger timed out waiting for child holon.
    /// Source: neurogenesis_monitor.
  | NeurogenesisTimeout { deadline_ms: Int, stressed_line: Int }
    /// Encoder output is not a valid density matrix.
    /// Source: SensoryEncoder.sense.
  | EncoderInvalid { modality: Text, trace: Float, min_eigenvalue: Float }
    /// Convergence not reached within budget.
    /// Source: sbd_step, phase_v1, phase_v2.
  | ConvergenceTimeout { steps_done: Int, loss: Float, target: Float };

\subsection{Application layer: the runtime}
\label{subsec:api-runtime}

\begin{lstlisting}[caption={\texttt{uhm\_runtime} main entry point.},label={lst:api-runtime}]
module uhm_runtime;

mount uhm_core.*;
mount uhm_lindblad.*;
mount uhm_cognitive.*;

public async fn main() -> Result<(), Text> using [ComputeDevice, Database] {
    // 1. Initialize the L0 level of the cognitive Kan complex
    let initial_gamma = density_fano_seed();
    let mut holon = atomic_holon(initial_gamma);

    // 2. Initialize concept-loading subsite
    let mut site = new_site();
    load_theory_from_yaml("theories/uhm.yaml", &mut site).await?;
    load_theory_from_yaml("theories/arithmetic.yaml", &mut site).await?;

    // 3. Construct the adjunction-descent dissipator/regeneration pair
    //    (Lemma lem:adjunction-descent, per-level Diss dashv Regen)
    let adj = AdjunctionDescent.new();

    // 4. Start the Giry oracle
    let oracle = GiryOracle {
        llm: None,
        smt: SmtSolver.z3(),
    };

    // 5. Start the environment stream
    let mut env = RealityStream.mock();

    // 6. Launch the steward tasks and the maturation loop inside one
    //    supervision nursery: the site steward OWNS `site`; everyone
    //    else holds only its channel handle (no shared locks anywhere).
    let config = MaturationConfig {
        dt: 0.01,
        c_target: 0.45,
        max_steps: 100_000,
    };

    nursery {
        let site_handle = spawn_site_steward(site);
        topological_maturation(
            &mut holon,
            site_handle,
            &oracle,
            &mut env,
            config,
        ).await?;
    }

    Ok(())
}
\end{lstlisting}

\subsection{Cog \texttt{uhm\_sensorimotor}}
\label{subsec:api-sensorimotor}

\begin{lstlisting}[caption={\texttt{uhm\_sensorimotor} public API.},label={lst:api-sensorimotor}]

    /// Observation dimension (fixed per modality at compile time).

    /// Encode raw observation into three-channel perturbation.
    /// This is pi_Gamma (Definition 12.3): the ontological projection
    /// functor sending a stream to a CPTP perturbation.
    fn sense(
        &self,
        observation: &[Float],
        gamma: &DensityMatrix7,
    ) -> Result<ThreeChannelPert, SynarcError>
        requires observation.len() == Self.OBS_DIM
        ensures result.is_ok() implies
            result.unwrap().h_hamiltonian.is_hermitian()
    ;

    /// Decode density matrix state into motor command.
    /// Implements Act functor (T-101 [T]): argmin over actions
    /// of max_k sigma_k^motor(Gamma(tau + delta_tau | a)).
    fn act(
        &self,
        gamma: &DensityMatrix7,
        rho_star: &DensityMatrix7,
    ) -> Result<List<Float>, SynarcError>;
};

// ============================================================================
// Concrete modality implementations
// ============================================================================

/// Vision modality: tensor input (H x W x C) -> pi_Gamma.
/// Encoder: linear projection R^D -> R^48 (Bloch vector) -> D(C^7)
/// via Cholesky normalization (categorically forced: encoder must
/// land in D(C^7), so last layer is always Cholesky + trace-normalize).
public type VisionModality is {
    encoder_weights: Matrix<Float>,   // D x 48, trained via SBD
    decoder_weights: Matrix<Float>,   // 48 x A, for motor output
    jacobian: Matrix<Float>,          // A x 48, body Jacobian
};

/// Audio modality: spectrogram input.
public type AudioModality is {
    encoder_weights: Matrix<Float>,
    decoder_weights: Matrix<Float>,
};

/// Proprioceptive modality: joint angles + forces.
public type ProprioModality is {
    encoder_weights: Matrix<Float>,
    decoder_weights: Matrix<Float>,
    jacobian: Matrix<Float>,
};

/// Language modality: token embedding input.
public type LanguageModality is {
    token_embeddings: Matrix<Float>,  // V x 48, vocabulary embeddings
    decoder_weights: Matrix<Float>,
};

// ============================================================================
// Modality registration (T-Modality-Closure: zero-touch addition)
// ============================================================================

public type ModalityRegistry is {
    modalities: Map<Text, Heap<dyn SensoryModality>>,
};

implement ModalityRegistry {
    public fn register(
        &mut self,
        name: Text,
        modality: Heap<dyn SensoryModality>,
    ) {
        self.modalities.insert(name, modality);
    }

    /// Apply all registered modalities to produce combined perturbation.
    /// Combination: weighted sum by modality salience (from sigma_k).
    public fn sense_all(
        &self,
        observations: &Map<Text, List<Float>>,
        gamma: &DensityMatrix7,
    ) -> Result<ThreeChannelPert, SynarcError>;
};

// ============================================================================
// Feedback stability (T-Feedback-Stability)
// ============================================================================

/// Verify that the closed sensorimotor loop preserves consciousness
/// within the stability radius r_stab = sqrt(P - P_crit).
public fn verify_feedback_stability(
    gamma: &DensityMatrix7,
    perturbation: &ThreeChannelPert,
    dt: Float,
) -> Bool
    requires gamma.purity() > P_CRIT + EPS
{
    // T-104 corrected 2026-08-07: sqrt(P - P_CRIT) is NOT the Bures radius
    // (it overstates by 2.6-48x, worst at the wall). Runtime form, <=1.13% error:
    let k = 0.925917;   // sqrt(35) * 6^(1/4) / 10
    let r_stab = k * ((gamma.purity() - 1.0/7.0).sqrt() - (1.0/7.0).sqrt());
    let pert_norm = perturbation.h_hamiltonian.frobenius_norm()
                  + perturbation.h_dissipator.frobenius_norm()
                  + perturbation.h_regenerator.frobenius_norm();
    pert_norm * dt < r_stab
}
\end{lstlisting}

\subsection{Development handoff: primitives required by the agentic cogs}
\label{subsec:api-agentic-primitives}

The agentic cogs of Appendices~\ref{app:active-inference},
\ref{app:morphology-design}, and \ref{app:memory-credit}
(\texttt{uhm\_active\_inference}, \texttt{uhm\_hierarchy},
\texttt{uhm\_memory}) call six helper primitives, specified here so a development
team can implement them without ambiguity. Each either refines an existing
\texttt{uhm\_core} operation or restricts a loop already defined in the body;
none introduces new mathematics.

\begin{notebox}[For the implementer --- the six helper contracts]
\textbf{\texttt{apply\_perturbation(gamma, dh) -> DensityMatrix7}} forms the
counterfactual next state $\hat{s} = \Gam \oplus \mathrm{d}h$ by applying the
three-channel Jacobian of Definition~\hyperref[def:three-channel]{12.1} to $\Gam$;
\texttt{ensures result.is\_density()}. It refines the three-channel action of
Section~\ref{sec:sensorimotor}.

\textbf{\texttt{bayes\_update(gamma, e) -> DensityMatrix7}} is the CPTP posterior
update $\mathcal{U}(\Gam \mid e)$ of Definition~\hyperref[def:three-tier]{N.1} (the
recursive Bayesian filter), a refinement of the standard-library L\"uders update
on \texttt{EpistemicState<7>}; \texttt{ensures result.is\_density()} and, on
dense evidence, agreement with the batch posterior (T-Memory-Sufficiency).

\textbf{\texttt{project\_to\_density(m) -> DensityMatrix7}} is the projection
$\Pi_{\Dens}$ of Definition~\hyperref[def:goal-inference]{L.4} (Hermitise, clip negative
eigenvalues, renormalise trace) onto $\Dens(\mathbb{C}^7)$ --- the non-expansive
nearest-density map; \texttt{ensures result.is\_density()}.

\textbf{\texttt{project\_sector\_ASD(gamma) -> DensityMatrix7}} is the sector
projector $\Pi_{\{A,S,D\}}$ onto the spatial reflex sector of
Proposition~\ref{prop:spatial-derived}: restrict to the $\{A,S,D\}$
rows/columns and renormalise; \texttt{ensures result.is\_density()}.

\textbf{\texttt{deliberate(holon, env) -> DensityMatrix7}} (async) is the
slow-loop setpoint computation of Definition~\hyperref[def:hierarchy]{M.2}: one
full-$\Gam$ / simplicial planning pass, implemented as an invocation of the
\texttt{topological\_maturation} cycle; it returns the deliberative setpoint (a
density).

\textbf{\texttt{reflex\_correct(holon, sector, setpoint, dtau, env)}} (async) is
one fast-loop step of Theorem~\hyperref[thm:hierarchical]{T-Hierarchical-Sensorimotor}: a single Section-12
sensorimotor step restricted to the $\{A,S,D\}$ sector, driving it toward
\texttt{setpoint} over period \texttt{dtau}; \texttt{ensures
holon.gamma.purity() > 2/7} (fast-loop viability).
\end{notebox}

\subsection{Summary}

The complete public API of \SYNARC{} consists of $\sim 100$ public
functions and $\sim 25$ public types, spread across the eight
cogs (\texttt{uhm\_core}, \texttt{uhm\_connes},
\texttt{uhm\_lindblad}, \texttt{uhm\_riemannian},
\texttt{uhm\_peps}, \texttt{uhm\_cognitive},
\texttt{uhm\_sensorimotor}, \texttt{uhm\_runtime}). Every function
carries a \texttt{requires}/\texttt{ensures} contract, verified by
the Verum SMT backend at compile time. The API is deliberately
small: anything not in this list either decomposes into these
primitives or is internal to a specific cog. The main runtime loop,
\texttt{topological\_maturation}, takes the simplicial cognitive
complex, the concept site, the Giry oracle, the environment, and
the configuration, and runs the seven-modality walk of
Section~\ref{subsec:maturation-cycle}.


CBGR Internals

This page is for compiler developers and anyone curious about the
mechanics. For the user-facing view, see
Language → CBGR.

Data structures

AllocationHeader

32 bytes, prepended to every CBGR-tracked allocation, 32-byte aligned
(one full cache line on x8664 / aarch64).

generation + epoch are laid out so they can be loaded in a single
64-bit atomic — loadgenerationepochcombined() does exactly that
on the fast path with Acquire ordering. Free uses Release on the
same word so reader visibility is guaranteed without a full fence.

ThinRef\

16 bytes. Used for sized T.

FatRef\

32 bytes. Used when T is unsized (slices, dyn) or for interior
references that need an offset into a larger allocation.

Check sequence

On x8664 this compiles to:

Measured: 55 cycles, ~13.8 ns on an M3 Max.

Allocator

Based on Mimalloc's segment architecture:

Segment: 32 MiB virtual region, lazily committed.
Page: subdivision of a segment; each page holds one size class.
Size class: 73 classes, spaced at 12.5% intervals, from 8 bytes
to 4 MiB.
LocalHeap: per-thread cache; lock-free fast path.
Free list: per-page, reversed on full page to maintain LIFO for
cache friendliness.

Freeing an object:
1. Atomically increments header.generation.
2. Pushes the slot onto the page's free list.

Concurrent readers are protected by hazard pointers (HazardGuard):
a reader installs its reference's target into a thread-local slot
before the CBGR check; a freer checks all slots before recycling the
memory.

Generation wraparound

Generations are 32-bit → wraparound at 4.29 billion allocations per
object. At 1 ns per alloc, that's ~4.3 seconds per object — a real
concern for tight loops that rapidly alloc/free.

Solution: epochs. Each thread advances a 32-bit epoch counter
periodically (every 1 ms, or on signal). References carry the epoch at
creation. When the allocator rolls a generation, it also advances the
page's epoch; any reference with an older epoch fails the check.

With 32-bit epochs rolled at 1 kHz per thread, wraparound is
effectively infinite for any practical workload.

Capability bits

The low 8 bits of the capabilities field (and the mirrored 8 bits in
ThinRef.epochcaps) encode a monotonically attenuating capability
set:

Monotonic attenuation: capabilities can only be removed as a
reference is passed around — a Database.readonly() transformation
clears CAPWRITE once and the result can never regain it. The
compiler enforces this at every conversion point.

A method dispatch for Database.write(...) emits a capability check:

The check is one AND + one branch — ~1 ns, dominated by the branch
predictor.

Compile-time analysis suite

The tier decisions that let the compiler emit &checked T or
&unsafe T instead of the Tier 0 &T come from a battery of
analyses in verumcbgr:

The pipeline walks references through each analysis, producing a
TierAnalysisResult that records decisions per RefId along with
statistics used for the optimiser's tier distribution report.

Promotion rule

Only references classified as NoEscape are eligible for SBGL
(stack-backed generation-less) promotion. MayEscape and Escapes
stay at Tier 0. When the purely syntactic analyses are inconclusive,
smtaliasverification.rs asks the SMT solver whether two references can alias
— proofs beyond "no" fall back to Tier 0 as well.

Typical promotion rate on idiomatic code: 60–95 % of &T occurrences
land at Tier 1.

Performance numbers (M3 Max)

VBC tier opcodes

Each tier is a distinct VBC instruction, so the tier decision is
visible all the way down to the bytecode — the interpreter and the
AOT lowering pipeline read the same opcode.

Tier behaviour across execution modes

The interpreter intentionally validates every deref regardless of
tier — it is the safe-by-default executor. Tier 1 and Tier 2 give
their 0 ns benefit under AOT, where the check is proven away
statically. Verum does not ship a JIT tier: the AOT pipeline lowers
VBC through LLVM (for CPU) and MLIR (for GPU), and the interpreter
handles every non-AOT execution path. A speculative baseline/JIT
tier was evaluated and removed as not pulling its weight given how
fast the interpreter already is and how effectively the AOT
pipeline elides tiered checks.

MLIR lowering

The verum.cbgr dialect mirrors the VBC opcodes:

Lowering strategy is one of:

CbgrValidated — Tier 0, emits a call into stdlib/mem's
validation function.
DirectLoad — Tier 1, lowers to llvm.load directly.
UncheckedLoad — Tier 2, lowers to llvm.load with no
metadata decorations.

Threads and concurrency

CBGR is designed to be lock-free on the fast path:

Per-thread local heap avoids contention.
Generations are atomic loads (no fences needed on x8664 TSO).
Hazard pointers replace epoch-based reclamation for finer-grained
safety.

On weakly-ordered architectures (aarch64), an acquire fence on deref
and a release fence on free provide the necessary ordering.

Analysis configuration knobs

CBGR ships a uniform configuration surface across every static
analysis pass. Every gate listed below is honoured by the
consumer code and pinned by a unit test inside the
corresponding analyser module — the user-facing contract is
"set the field, observe the difference".

The configs share a uniform shape:

Each Config carries production-suitable defaults.
Where the same config has multiple stances (aggressive vs
conservative vs disabled), factory constructors expose them.
Where a result struct exists, it mirrors the config booleans
through () accessors so diagnostic builders never need to
re-read the analyser's internal state.
minconfidence-style threshold fields filter every warning
class identically (one filter pass per detector, applied
centrally).
max cap fields with default 0 mean "unlimited"; any
positive value bounds the analysis cost at the price of
potentially missing entries in the truncated tail (documented
inline in the analyser source).

LifetimeAnalysisConfig

NllConfig

Convenience constructors:

ConcurrencyAnalysisConfig

EnhancedContextConfig (context-sensitive analysis)

The convenience constructor EnhancedContextConfig::allenabled()
flips the three booleans to true and keeps the depth defaults
(3 / 10). Calling withconfig(EnhancedContextConfig::allenabled())
on a fresh ContextSensitiveAnalyzer::new() now produces the
same effective shape as the bespoke withallenhancements()
constructor — depthpolicy + compressor are auto-installed.

ParallelConfig (context-sensitive parallel analysis)

ValueTrackingConfig (concrete-value tracking for escape refinement)

The three domain gates are independent — opting out of constant
tracking keeps symbolic and range tracking active (and vice-versa)
so callers can build a precise per-analysis cost / precision
profile. The configuration is passed when constructing a
ValuePropagator or driving the enhanced escape analyser; both
honour the same ValueTrackingConfig shape and propagate the
gates uniformly through their worklist.

Code Generation

verumcodegen translates VBC bytecode into native machine code via
two backends: LLVM for ahead-of-time CPU compilation, and
MLIR for the GPU path (@device(gpu) functions, tensor
kernels). Neither is a JIT; Verum has two and only two execution
modes, the VBC interpreter and the AOT-lowered native binary.
Everything verumcodegen produces is compiled ahead of time.

LLVM backend

Located in verumcodegen::llvm. Organised by concern: instruction
lowering (instruction.rs), VBC translation (vbclowering.rs),
runtime helpers (runtime.rs), FFI trampolines (ffi.rs), tensor /
SIMD intrinsic mapping (tensorir.rs, simd.rs), platform-specific
IR (platformir.rs), and target-triple gating
(targettriple.rs).

VBC → LLVM IR

vbclowering.rs walks VBC functions and emits LLVM IR:

Values become SSA registers.
Control flow maps to LLVM basic blocks + br / br-cond.
Function calls map to call / invoke (the latter for
exception-propagating contexts).
CBGR checks lower to a load-compare-branch sequence, then
optimised by LLVM's passes.
Cubical opcodes lower to identity / noop (proof erasure).

Runtime support

runtime.rs generates:
CBGR helper functions (fast-path open-coded inline; slow-path
emitted as IR helpers in the same module).
Allocation entry points: every Heap(...) lowers to a wrapper
that calls verumosalloc / verumosfree, themselves emitted
by platformir.rs against mmap / munmap on Unix and
VirtualAlloc / VirtualFree on Windows. There is no libc
allocator in the dependency chain — see
no-libc architecture.
Context stack primitives (push, pop, lookup).
Panic and unwind machinery.

FFI trampolines

ffi.rs emits trampolines for extern "C" functions:
Argument marshalling (Verum types ↔ C types).
Return value handling.
Exception conversion (C errno / return codes → Verum Result).
CBGR guarding of outgoing pointers (wrapped as &unsafe T).

Tensor and SIMD

tensorir.rs and simd.rs map tensor and SIMD opcodes to platform
intrinsics — SSE / AVX / AVX-512 on x8664, NEON on aarch64, scalar
fallbacks on other targets. Tensor ops that have a fused intrinsic
form on the target (flash attention, layer norm, …) are kept as a
single op all the way down so vendor intrinsics can be emitted
directly rather than reconstructed from primitive linalg.

GPU (Metal)

metalir.rs emits Metal shading-language IR for @kernel
functions.

Inline assembly

asm.rs supports @llvmonly unsafe asm!(...) for kernels and
drivers. Bitfield layout is handled by bitfield.rs for
memory-mapped I/O.

MLIR backend

Located in verumcodegen::mlir. Used for autodiff lowering and the
GPU path (@device(gpu) functions and tensor kernels). The LLVM
backend handles CPU AOT; MLIR owns the GPU target family.

MLIR is invoked only at AOT compile time. There is no
just-in-time compilation in Verum — GPU kernels are compiled to
their target IR (PTX, HSACO, SPIR-V, Metal AIR) during verum
build and embedded into the final executable. The runtime looks a
kernel up by ID and launches it; it never invokes MLIR.

Dialect stack

VBC lowers progressively through a fixed ladder of dialects:

Passes in passes/ drive each lowering step. Standard dialects
(arith, cf, math, memref) handle the plumbing; verum.tensor
keeps high-level shape information alive long enough for fusion
passes to run before dropping to linalg.

VBC → dialect mapping (selected)

Flash attention stays a single op all the way to the target — the
lowering emits vendor intrinsics directly rather than reconstructing
the pattern from linalg.

GPU targets

Four backends share the MLIR pipeline. The canonical mapping is
the GpuTarget enum in
crates/verumcodegen/src/mlir/vbclowering.rs — every row below
is a direct projection of that enum's targettriple() /
dialect() / memoryspace() accessors:

Two natural partitions on the GpuTarget surface:

Device-global memory (memoryspace == 1): CUDA + ROCm.
These targets carry a separate device address space; memref
attributes pin allocations into device global memory.
Host-shared memory (memoryspace == 0): Vulkan + Metal.
Address-space 0 is the default; the host-shared model lets
CPU and GPU access the same allocation without an explicit
copy. A wrong classification on this axis silently miscompiles
memref attributes — pinned by the metapingputargetround
tripuniqueandclassification test in the lowering crate.

Matmul tile sizes are picked per-launch by the
gpu.lower-matmul-tile MLIR pass based on detected device
capability rather than declared statically per target — the
numbers vary with CUDA SM version, ROCm CDNA variant, Vulkan
driver, and Metal GPU family, and are not enumerable as a
single-row-per-target table.

AOT compilation

aot/ runs the full pass pipeline and emits an object file linked
alongside the LLVM-produced host code. Every GPU kernel in a Verum
binary is produced this way — during verum build, never at
runtime. The output is a target-specific binary (PTX, HSACO,
SPIR-V, or Metal AIR) embedded into the executable and loaded by
the runtime on first kernel launch.

Caching

Compiled kernel binaries are cached keyed by
(vbcfingerprint, target, optlevel) so an incremental rebuild
touches only the kernels whose VBC actually changed. First-build
times vary by target (~50 ms per kernel for NVPTX on modern
hardware) but are paid once per edit, not per program run.

Why JIT is not a production execution tier

Verum's two production execution tiers are the VBC interpreter
(Tier 0) and the AOT-compiled native binary (Tier 1). An MLIR
ExecutionEngine-backed JIT exists as the experimental
CompilationMode::MlirJit mode (see pipeline.rs::CompilationMode
pipeline/mlir.rs::JitEngine) — its primary use case is hot-reload
during interactive development and incremental rebuild, not
shipping production code.

The reasoning for keeping JIT off the production tier list:

The interpreter already starts in milliseconds and handles the
full VBC instruction set (including cubical, HoTT, and autodiff
opcodes that a JIT would have to recompile every time the type
checker changes).
The AOT path produces native code that matches or beats a JIT's
peak performance once warmed up — there is no warm-up to avoid
because the interpreter fills the no-AOT-step role.
Promoting JIT to a third production tier would double the
combinatorial surface of the backend (interpreter × JIT × AOT,
each with its own CBGR-tier lowerings) without targeting a use
case that neither of the existing two already covers.

The retained JIT infrastructure under crates/verumcodegen/src/
mlir/jit/ (engine, hot-reload, incremental, REPL, symbol
resolver) is reachable only by selecting the experimental
MlirJit compilation mode explicitly; the canonical
verum run / verum build flows route through Interpreter /
AOT respectively.

GPU binaries

gpubinary.rs assembles Metal .metallib, SPIR-V modules, or PTX /
HSACO blobs from MLIR-lowered kernels and embeds them into the final
executable via the linker's TEXT,const section (macOS) or a
dedicated .rodata.verumgpu section (Linux / Windows). The runtime
looks them up by kernel ID at launch time; the launch path has no
dependency on a live MLIR context.

Autodiff lowering

@differentiable functions go through a source-transformation pass
that runs on the MLIR side so VJP rules can be expressed over
linalg ops rather than bytecode:

1. The primal function is lowered to verum.tensor as usual.
2. A reverse-mode pass walks the op graph and emits a companion
function using VJP rules registered per op.
3. Tape storage (for activations that the backward pass needs) uses
a stack-allocated GradientTape when possible, falling back to
Heap when shapes are dynamic.

The GradientTape context sees every linalg op, so the backward
pass fuses into the forward kernel whenever the dataflow allows
(saving a materialisation of the primal output).

Linking

link.rs drives the in-tree LLD wrapper (verumllvmsys::lld) and
applies a no-libc linking configuration on every platform:

Linux: lld (ELF flavour). No libc, no libm, no libpthread —
the runtime calls direct syscalls.
macOS: lld (Mach-O flavour) linking only libSystem.B.dylib,
Apple's required boundary.
Windows: lld-link linking only ntdll.dll + kernel32.dll
— no MSVC CRT, no UCRT.
FreeBSD: lld (ELF flavour) with direct syscalls.
Cross-compilation: every per-platform codegen decision reads the
target triple, never the host's cfg(targetos) — see
no-libc architecture for
what that guarantees and what is still open. verum does not
bundle sysroots or cross-linkers; the final link needs the target's
own toolchain, installed separately.

LTO options:
thin (default): fast, good inlining.
full: slower, maximum cross-module optimisation.

See no-libc architecture
for the full ruleset and the per-platform link-audit procedure
(ldd / otool / dumpbin).

Debug information

DWARF on Linux / macOS.
PDB on Windows.
Source-level debugging: variables, types, expressions.
CBGR header awareness: debuggers can pretty-print generation and
epoch.

Artefact layout

.cog is a library artefact: VBC + metadata + optional proof certs.

See also

VBC bytecode — the input to
codegen.
Runtime tiers — when each
backend runs.
Language → FFI — user-facing FFI boundary.



Compilation Pipeline

The compiler has a VBC-first architecture: every program lowers
to VBC bytecode, and VBC is either interpreted (Tier 0) or compiled
to native code via LLVM (Tier 1). Orchestration lives in
verumcompiler::pipeline::Pipeline.

High-level shape

Phase map

MIR is not in the main pipeline
The compiler contains MIR infrastructure, but it is only used by the
verification and advanced optimisation subsystems (SMT
obligation generation, refinement-aware bounds elimination). The main
compilation path goes TypedAST → VBC → execution, never through
MIR.

Phase 0 — Stdlib preparation

Compiles core/ modules once per build and caches stdlib metadata
for the type checker and VBC codegen. The persistent disk cache
(target/.verum-cache/stdlib/) keys on content hash, so unrelated
edits never invalidate stdlib artefacts. verum check skips this
phase entirely — signatures come directly from built-ins.

Phase 1 — Lexical & parsing

Tokenisation via verumlexer (logos-generated DFA).
Recursive-descent parsing via verumfastparser → a lossless
green-tree AST preserving comments and whitespace.
Entry-point discovery (main, @test, @bench).

File-level parsing parallelises across cores.

Phase 2 — Meta registry & AST registration

Registers every @derive, tagged-literal handler, @verify
attribute, and user-defined meta fn into a global MetaRegistry.
This makes Phase 3 order-independent — a macro can refer to a type
defined later in the same file.

Phase 3 — Macro expansion & literal processing

Procedural macros (@derive, @metamacro-registered functions).
Tagged-literal parsing (json#, sql#, rx#, url#, …). Each
tag validates its content at compile time; invalid content is a
compile error, not a runtime failure.
quote / splice / lift hygiene enforcement (see
metaprogramming).

Contract literals (contract#"...") are parsed here and verified in
Phase 3a.

Phase 3a — Contract verification

Collects contract obligations from contract# literals.
Translates to SMT-LIB via verumsmt::exprtosmtlib.
Dispatches to a single solver or the portfolio executor per the
function's @verify(...) mode.
Fails the build with a counter-example on violation.

This runs between Phase 3 and Phase 4 because a contract's proof may
reference reflected predicates registered in Phase 2 but must be
discharged before the type checker sees the annotated function.

Phase 4 — Semantic analysis

Bidirectional inference (verumtypes::infer).
Refinement types — narrowed by flow analysis where possible;
unresolved predicates become SMT obligations at this phase. The
DependentVerifier runs here, as a sub-step of semantic analysis,
not as a later phase of its own.
Context clauses — using ... resolved; capability subtyping
checked.
CBGR analysis — every &T receives a tier annotation
(managed / checked / unsafe) through the multi-module
reference-analysis suite documented in
cbgr internals.
Cubical bridge — Type.Eq values translated via
verumtypes::cubicalbridge to cubical terms before unification.

Verification results that feed later phases are produced here as
the Phase 4 refinement / DependentVerifier sub-step, which
together with the Phase 3a contract sub-step covers everything
the SMT layer is asked to discharge. See
verification pipeline
for the solver-side internals.

Phase 4a — Autodiff compilation

For every @differentiable fn, builds the computational graph and
synthesises a VJP (vector-Jacobian product) companion. See
math → autodiff
for the user-facing API; the transformation runs on MLIR
verum.tensor ops so VJPs can fuse with the forward kernel.

Phase 4b — Context-system validation

Validates that every using ... clause has a matching provide
on every call path, enforces capability attenuation, and rejects
forbidden contexts declared via !IO-style negative constraints.

Also runs Send/Sync enforcement for values crossing spawn.

extern "C" / ffi contracts are validated here — boundary
contracts (memoryeffects, errorsvia, @ownership) must be
consistent with the declared signature.

Phases 4a and 4b run in parallel after Phase 4's core type checking.

Phase 5 — VBC code generation

phases/vbccodegen.rs lowers TypedAST to VBC bytecode function by
function. Every function in the program — stdlib included — ends up
as VBC.

Opcodes: the ~200-opcode VBC instruction set
(see vbc bytecode).
CBGR opcodes: Tier-aware lowering emits Ref / RefMut for
Tier 0 references, RefChecked for Tier 1 (compiler-proven safe),
and RefUnsafe for Tier 2.
Cubical erasure: path, transport, and univalence terms lower
to identity / no-op (proof erasure is enabled by default via
codegen prooferasure = true).

Phase 6 — VBC monomorphization

Generic functions specialise per concrete argument types. Duplicate
instantiations dedupe via structural hashing, and the
monomorphisation cache (codegen monomorphizationcache = true)
reuses specialisations across incremental builds.

Phase 7 — Execution (two-tier model v2.1)

Tier 0 — interpretation

phaseinterpret runs the VBC directly with full safety checks.
Used by verum run (default), verum test, verum bench, the
Playbook TUI, and meta fn evaluation inside Phases 2–4.

Tier 1 — AOT

runnativecompilation lowers VBC → LLVM IR via
verumcodegen::llvm::VbcToLlvmLowering, runs LLVM's optimisation
pipeline, emits object files, and hands off to Phase 7.5 linking
below. Triggered by verum build, verum run --aot, or
profile.release tier = "1".

Worker fence before LLVM
LLVM initialises its back-end pass registry lazily via
function-local statics. To keep that initialisation race-free
across the parallel phase pool, the pipeline initialises the
target on the main thread before any worker is spawned, then
issues a fan-out / fan-in barrier just before codegen so every
worker has finished its prior phase by the time LLVM is touched.
This keeps repeated AOT builds deterministic on every supported
host.

Dual-path: GPU via MLIR

Functions annotated @device(GPU) (or auto-selected when tensor
ops exceed a cost threshold) go through
verumcodegen::mlir::VbcToMlirGpuLowering instead: VBC →
verum.tensor → linalg → gpu → PTX / HSACO / SPIR-V / Metal.
MLIR is only used for GPU — CPU code always goes through LLVM.

Phase 7.5 — Final linking (AOT only)

Static linking via embedded LLD — Verum ships its own linker.

No-libc freestanding: the runtime is implemented in Verum's
own intrinsics; no glibc / musl / MSVC CRT dependency. macOS is
the one exception, where libSystem.B.dylib is Apple's stable
ABI entry point and the only acceptable boundary. See
no-libc architecture.
LLD flavours: ELF (Linux, FreeBSD), Mach-O (macOS), COFF
(Windows).
LTO: thin by default (configurable in linker / lto).
Targets: x8664, aarch64, riscv64, wasm32, plus embedded
profiles such as thumbv7em and riscv32imac.

Parallelisation strategy

Incremental compilation

See incremental compilation
for the full strategy. Key points:

Fingerprinting: source + type + dependency + config hash per
function.
Cache location: target/.verum-cache/ /.
Hit rate: 10–15× faster rebuild after a one-function edit on
50 K-LOC projects.

Pipeline diagnostics

Cold start — the part that is not your program

The per-phase numbers above are what your code costs. Separately from
them, every invocation pays a fixed amount to make the standard library
available: the compiler ships a precompiled bytecode archive with its
typecheck metadata and its call-graph index, and those are loaded before
your source is looked at.

This floor is why a four-line program does not compile in four lines'
worth of time, and why a throughput figure (LOC/second on a large module)
and a small program's wall-clock are two different measurements. Quote
both, and measure them separately: throughput on a large input, cold
start on an empty main.

What moves the floor, in the order that matters:

What your program names. The loader walks the call graph from the
names your module references and decodes only the archive entries it
reaches. A program that touches nothing loads a handful of entries; one
that constructs a List loads more; mount core. loads a great deal
(see modules).
The call-graph index is precomputed at build time and read as
bytes, so it is not rebuilt per invocation.
Typecheck metadata is decoded on first use, not per file.

If you are chasing a slow build, separate the two before optimising:
compile an empty main to see the floor, then your real module. If the
empty one is most of the time, the fix is not in your code.

Breadcrumbs on failure

Every phase pushes an RAII breadcrumb (verumerror::breadcrumb) so
that if the pipeline panics or crashes with a fatal signal, the
emitted report at ~/.verum/crashes/ names the last phase that was
running and its per-phase context (file being compiled, module name,
etc.). See Tooling → Crash diagnostics
for the report layout and the verum diagnose workflow.
